# Universal monolithic primitive firewall after Formation v10

Forge v0.1 inherited the v8/v9 one-factor and two-factor primitive-atom results and therefore treated architectures with more than two nonabelian composition factors as outside the proved firewall.  Formation Polarization v10 corrects that frontier.

For every class C of finite groups,

NMP(Form(C)) = union_{G in C} P_na(G),

where the left side is the set of nonabelian monolithic primitive action types occurring in the generated formation and P_na(G) is the palette attached to nonabelian chief factors of the original generators.

Therefore the Wilson Forge no longer needs a composition-length gate at the monolithic primitive level.  Arbitrarily many nonabelian modules may be composed by ordinary formation generation without creating a new nonabelian monolithic primitive action type that was absent from every generator.

This is stronger than the v0.1 atom firewall and supersedes it.

The boundary is equally important: v10 does not say that all cooperative nonsoluble structure disappears.  Non-monolithic primitive and formation-critical groups may retain several minimal normal blocks simultaneously.  That cooperative layer is the correct remaining finite-group frontier and must not be silently identified with monolithic primitive-spectrum preservation.

For the master architecture this gives a clean rule: monolithic primitive type is globally palette-safe under arbitrary formation composition; any new analysis burden begins only when the application asks about cooperative multi-minimal-normal structure rather than a single associated chief-factor primitive action.
